products.name: AEM Forms
products.title: Experience Manager Forms as a Cloud Service
products.what: A cloud-native service to create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms and send the submitted data to back-end systems, with APIs that generate documents from templates and data.

source.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

products.notes: Adobe recommends Adaptive Forms Core Components for new forms, and these lines assume them. The service keeps no submitted data in AEM: every form sends its data to a store your client owns, and AEM workflows run on Author only. Document generation (the Communications APIs) is its own add-on that Adobe enables on request, licensed by Document Renditions, and one API call or batch takes one template. The Automated Forms Conversion service produces Foundation Components forms, and the in-form Acrobat Sign fields are documented for Foundation Components only, so AF08 signs through a workflow step. Acrobat Sign and Adobe Analytics are not products in the tool, so e-signature (AF08) and form analytics (AF09) are product lines with an ext. Adobe's pages disagree with each other on XFA-based adaptive forms, HTML5 Forms and document security on the Cloud Service; see left_out and the research trail before quoting any of them. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none. AF18 (Nov 10, Adam: yes to an accessibility service) rests on Adobe's accessible forms page, which Adobe files under Foundation Components; its five checks (accessible names, labels, text equivalents, contrast, keyboard) are what the service reviews, and the Core Components introduction says those components support accessibility standards and guidelines. The service promises a review and fixes, not a conformance certificate.
prereqs: An AEM as a Cloud Service program with the Forms solution switched on in Cloud Manager (Solutions & Add-ons) and the build pipeline run afterwards
An AEM Forms license sized in Form Submissions per year (adaptive forms) or Document Renditions per year (document generation)
For document generation: the Renditions entitlement, since a Submissions license does not include Document Rendition features
A data store your client owns for submitted data (database, REST service, SharePoint, Azure Blob Storage and similar), because no submit action stores data in AEM
Users added to the Forms groups on Author and Publish, such as forms-users, template-authors, fdm-authors and workflow-editors
Up to 20 concurrent users on Author with a license up to 750,000 Form Submissions a year (40 at 750,000 or more)
One production, one stage, one development and one rapid development environment in the base package

tiers.name: Forms - Digital Enrollment
tiers.what: The Cloud Manager solution option that switches on adaptive forms. Lines AF01 to AF11 and AF16 to AF17 assume it.
tiers.quote: You can use Forms as a Cloud Service to create an adaptive form (Digital Enrollment) or generate a customer communication.

tiers.name: Forms - Communications (shown as Forms - Communications Add-On where Digital Enrollment is already on)
tiers.what: The Cloud Manager option that switches on the Communications APIs for document generation and manipulation, on its own or added to Digital Enrollment. Adobe enables access on request. Lines AF12 to AF15 need it.
tiers.quote: Communications capability is available as a standalone and add-on module for Forms as a Cloud Service users.

tiers.name: AEM Forms: Submissions (license)
tiers.what: The base package licensed by Form Submissions per year. It does not include Document Rendition features; those need the Renditions add-on.
tiers.quote: Customer's license to AEM Forms Submissions does not include a license to use Document Rendition features and functionality, which requires purchasing the AEM Forms Additional Renditions (Document Renditions) add-on.

tiers.name: AEM Forms: Renditions (license)
tiers.what: The base package licensed by Document Renditions per year. It does not include Form Submission features, and the Automated Forms Conversion service needs the Submissions add-on.
tiers.quote: Customer's license to AEM Forms Renditions does not include a license to use Form Submission features and functionality, which requires purchasing the AEM Forms Additional Submissions (Form Submissions) add-on.

tiers.name: AEM Forms: EDS Submissions Add-on to Sites
tiers.what: A limited forms add-on for AEM Sites clients on Edge Delivery: 15 fields per submission, and no Forms Designer, Automated Forms Conversion, Document of Record, e-signature integrations or workflows.
tiers.quote: does not include use of AEM Forms Designer (desktop and cloud versions), Automated Forms Conversion Service, or the following extensions related to processing of submitted forms: Document of Record, e-signature integrations, and workflows

lines.name: Forms onboarding, project setup and access
lines.scope: Enable the Forms solution on your client's Cloud Manager program (Forms - Digital Enrollment, plus the Communications add-on where documents are generated), run the build pipeline, add users to the Forms groups on Author and Publish, and set up the local SDK and the Archetype project developers deploy from.
lines.evidence: After completing Onboarding to the Adobe Experience Manager as a Cloud Service, perform the following actions to enable Forms - Digital Enrollment or Customer Communications features

source.title: Experience League: Onboard to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Form templates, themes and fragments
lines.scope: Build the Adaptive Form templates, the theme that carries your client's brand and the reusable fragments (such as name and address panels) that every form starts from, on Core Components.
lines.evidence: With Template Editor, you can create a template that contains basic structure and initial content that authors can use to create forms.

source.title: Experience League: Build an Adaptive Form template with Core Components

lines.name: Adaptive form build with rules
lines.scope: Build your client's first adaptive forms on Core Components (as a guide, one long multi-step application or about five short forms): panels and steps, fields, validation, and the rules that show, hide, calculate and call services.
lines.evidence: AEM Forms' form builder lets you create forms that are engaging, responsive, dynamic, and adaptive.

source.title: Experience League: Form builder: Create forms with core components

lines.name: Form Data Model for back-end systems
lines.scope: Configure your client's data sources (REST, SOAP or OData services, or a relational database) and build the Form Data Model that prefills forms from the case or records system and writes submitted data back to it.
lines.evidence: AEM Forms Data Integration allows configuring and connecting disparate data sources with AEM Forms.

source.title: Experience League: Connect AEM Forms to a database

lines.name: Submit actions and server-side validation
lines.scope: Set each form's submit action (REST endpoint, Form Data Model, email, SharePoint, Azure Blob Storage or an AEM workflow) so data lands in a store your client owns, add a custom submit action where needed, and turn on server-side revalidation.
lines.evidence: A submit action is triggered when a user clicks the Submit button on an Adaptive Form. Forms as a Cloud Service provides several submit actions out of the box.

source.title: Experience League: Submit Actions Supported by Adaptive Forms

lines.name: Submission PDF for each form
lines.scope: Set up the Submission PDF (Document of Record) that keeps a print-friendly record of each submitted form: auto-generated, or on a branded XDP template built in Forms Designer and bound to the form's fields.
lines.evidence: To create a Submission PDF, an XFA or Acroform based template is merged with data collected via an adaptive form.

source.title: Experience League: Generate a Submission PDF (Document of Record) for Adaptive Forms (Core Components)

lines.name: Review and approval workflows
lines.scope: Build the AEM Workflow models that start when a form is submitted: assign review tasks to people or groups in the AEM Inbox, route approvals and rejections, send email notifications, and keep sensitive workflow data in your client's own storage.
lines.evidence: The assign task step creates a work item and assigns it to a user or group.

source.title: Experience League: Use Forms-centric AEM Workflows - Step Reference to automate business processes

lines.name: E-signature with Acrobat Sign
lines.scope: Create the Acrobat Sign API application and the Acrobat Sign cloud configuration on Author and Publish, then add signing to your client's process with the Sign Document workflow step: the signers, the signing order and the signed document.
lines.evidence: Adobe Acrobat Sign enables e-signature workflows for Adaptive Forms and AEM Workflows.

source.title: Experience League: Connect AEM Forms as a Cloud Service with Adobe Acrobat Sign

lines.name: Form analytics with Adobe Analytics
lines.scope: Set up a Tags property with the Adobe Experience Manager Forms and Adobe Analytics extensions, the data elements and rules for form events and the report suite mapping, then build your client's report on renders, submissions, errors and abandonment.
lines.evidence: When an event occurs on an adaptive form, AEM Forms send these data elements to Adobe Analytics.

source.title: Experience League: Form Analytics with Adobe Analytics and AEM Forms - Complete Guide

lines.name: PDF form conversion to adaptive forms
lines.scope: Connect the Automated Forms Conversion service, convert your client's existing PDF forms (AcroForms, XFA-based or non-interactive) in batches within the service's size limits, then review and correct each converted form and apply your client's template and theme. The service produces forms on Foundation Components, the earlier of Adobe's two component sets for adaptive forms, so converted forms are maintained with that set's editor.
lines.evidence: The above conversion settings apply to converting PDF forms to Foundation Components-based adaptive forms.

source.title: Experience League: Convert PDF forms to adaptive forms

lines.name: Migration from AEM 6.5 Forms
lines.scope: Move your client's forms from AEM 6.5 Forms on OSGi: run the Best Practices Analyzer, make forms, themes, templates and cloud configurations compatible with the Migration Utility on a cloned environment, then transfer them with the Content Transfer Tool.
lines.evidence: You can migrate or upgrade your Adaptive Forms, themes, templates, and cloud configurations from AEM 6.5 Forms on OSGi to AEM as a Cloud Service.

source.title: Experience League: Migrate from AEM Forms (On-Premise and AMS environments) to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Form accessibility review
lines.scope: Review your client's forms against the accessibility standard your client names, such as WCAG or Section 508, using the checks Adobe lists for form authors: an accessible name and description on every control, proper labels, text equivalents for images, sufficient color contrast and keyboard access. Test each form with an accessibility inspection tool, correct what the form's settings and theme control, and report what needs custom development.
lines.evidence: While authoring an Adaptive Form, form authors must address the following considerations to build an accessible Adaptive Form

source.title: Experience League: Creating accessible Adaptive Forms

lines.name: Document templates in Forms Designer
lines.scope: Create your client's letter, notice and document templates as XDP form designs in Forms Designer, define the XML data each one merges, and upload them to the Forms instance, including templates that replace a legacy system's output.
lines.evidence: Typically, you create a template using Designer and use Communications APIs to merge data with the template.

source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

lines.name: On-demand document generation
lines.scope: Set up server-to-server credentials and connect your client's application to the synchronous Communications APIs, so a letter or PDF is generated from a template and data the moment a form is submitted or a case worker asks for it.
lines.evidence: Synchronous APIs are suitable for on-demand, low latency, and single record document generation scenarios.

source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

lines.name: Batch document generation
lines.scope: Connect your client's Microsoft Azure Storage, create the batch data store and the batch configurations, and set up the scheduled runs from your client's application that turn a set of records into PDF or print documents.
lines.evidence: Communication APIs use customer owned Microsoft Azure Cloud storage to fetch customer records and store generated documents.

lines.name: PDF/A output and document assembly
lines.scope: Add the document steps your client's records policy needs: convert generated PDFs to PDF/A and validate them, and assemble or split document packages with DDX, including the Dispatcher rule those APIs need.
lines.evidence: You can use the APIs to convert a PDF document to a PDF/A-compliant document and also to determine whether a PDF document is PDF/A-compliant.

source.title: Experience League: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service Communication APIs

lines.name: Training for authors, developers and administrators
lines.scope: Train your client's team by role: form practitioners on building, styling and publishing forms, developers on custom components, workflows and the local SDK, and administrators on users, groups, data sources and configurations, with a handover guide.

lines.name: PDF and XDP imports with Coworker
lines.scope: Store your client's existing PDF and XDP forms in the AEM DAM, import them into adaptive forms with Coworker, then review each form's fields, rules and layout in the editor.
lines.evidence: Convert a PDF or XDP stored in AEM DAM into an Adaptive Form.

source.title: Experience League: Forms Agentic Capabilities

not_documented.why: Indirect only. The Cloud Service docs have no page that sets up Forms with Target; the mentions are that a form built inside an AEM Sites page can use that page's targeting, and a line in the form analytics guide that names Target for form A/B testing without any setup steps. Adobe's Forms FAQ also lists integration with Adobe Target among the features left out of the first Cloud Service release. Treat it as an AEM Sites and Target matter (aemsites-target), not a Forms connection.
not_documented.quote: Targeting (Integration with Adobe Target): With AEM Sites pages targeting capabilities, you can also personalize the form experience for different audiences

not_documented.why: Tutorial only. One Experience League tutorial shows a form submission updating a profile, a Journey Optimizer journey starting, and a custom action calling AEM Forms APIs to generate a document. No product page describes a Forms and Journey Optimizer integration, and the tutorial relies on Interactive Communication, which Adobe's notable changes page assigns to AEM 6.5 Forms.
not_documented.quote: This use case demonstrates how AEM Forms and Adobe Journey Optimizer can work together to automate the generation and delivery of personalized communications based on customer interests captured through a form submission.

left_out.what: Adaptive forms (Core Components) built from XFA or XDP form templates
left_out.why: Adobe's page puts it under its early adopter program. Adobe's pages also disagree: the notable changes page says the service does not support XFA-based Adaptive Forms, while the FAQ says they can be created on Cloud Service instances.
left_out.quote: The feature is available under early adopter program.

left_out.what: Automated Forms Conversion straight to Core Components forms
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program. AF10 therefore covers the generally documented route, which produces Foundation Components forms; the Review and Correct editor is not available for Core Components output.
left_out.quote: The above conversion settings apply to converting PDF forms to Foundation Components-based adaptive forms.

left_out.what: Submission PDF for forms created inside AEM Sites pages, and locale-specific XDP templates for it
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program, so AF06 covers standalone adaptive forms only.
left_out.quote: Submission PDF configuration for forms embedded in AEM Sites pages and locale-specific custom XDP templates for Document of Record are under the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Uploading generated PDFs straight to Azure Blob Storage from the document generation API
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program. AF13 returns the document to your client's application instead.
left_out.quote: Uploading the generated PDFs using document generation API to Azure Blob Storage capability is under Early Adopter Program

left_out.what: Document Extraction APIs (PDF properties, usage rights, metadata)
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program.
left_out.quote: The Document Extraction capability is under the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Convert PDF to XDP, and the HTML to PDF, PostScript to PDF, PDF to image, PDF to PostScript and flatten transparency conversions
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program. A legacy template therefore has no documented automatic conversion to XDP: AF12 creates templates in Forms Designer.
left_out.quote: The HTML to PDF, PostScript to PDF, PDF to Image, PDF to PostScript, and Flatten Transparency APIs are under the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Interactive Communications authoring and the Agent UI (business users composing correspondence)
left_out.why: Adobe's notable changes page assigns Interactive Communications and Agent UI use cases to an AEM 6.5 Forms environment, and the Interactive Communication Editor items on the Cloud Service sit in the Early Access list. AF12 to AF14 cover correspondence through templates and the Communications APIs.
left_out.quote: You can use an AEM 6.5 Forms environment for Interactive Communications and Agent UI use-cases.

left_out.what: Theme Editor for Core Components adaptive forms
left_out.why: Listed in Adobe's Early Access Program, so AF02 customizes a theme in code (Canvas, WKND or EASEL as the base).
left_out.quote: Style Core Components based Adaptive Forms visually in the Theme Editor and preview changes as you work.

left_out.what: Virus scanning or validation of file attachments
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program.
left_out.quote: The File Attachment Virus Scanner / Validator capability is under the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Direct API integration in the Visual Rule Editor, and REST services configured by Service Endpoint
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program. AF04 uses the Form Data Model for service calls.
left_out.quote: Integrating API in Rule Editor is under Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Configurable tables in Core Components adaptive forms
left_out.why: Under Adobe's early adopter program.
left_out.quote: The feature is available under the early adopter program.

left_out.what: Compare Adaptive Forms
left_out.why: Adobe's page calls it a pre-release feature.
left_out.quote: This is a pre-release feature and accessible through our pre-release channel

left_out.what: Forms Experience Builder (the AI assistant inside the Adaptive Forms editor)
left_out.why: Adobe's pages disagree: the deploy and how-to pages say it is available under an early access program, while its FAQ says it is now generally available. Left out until Adobe's pages agree.
left_out.quote: The Forms Experience Builder is available under an early access program.

left_out.what: Rule Editor and form fragments for Edge Delivery forms in the Universal Editor
left_out.why: The Universal Editor interface page labels the Rule Editor (Early Access), and the overview page labels Form Fragments (Coming Soon), although both have how-to pages. AFX04 scopes form creation and publishing only.
left_out.quote: Rule Editor (Early Access) Purpose: Add dynamic behaviors, validations, and conditional logic

left_out.what: Conversational Forms and Agentic Form Filling
left_out.why: Both are listed in Adobe's Early Access Program.
left_out.quote: Agentic Form Filling lets customers complete published Adaptive Forms through AI assistants, website chatbots, or WhatsApp.

left_out.what: Document expiration for Acrobat Sign agreements
left_out.why: Under Adobe's Early Adopter Program.
left_out.quote: Setting document expiration for Adobe Sign agreements is under the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Forms Service APIs (interactive PDF forms rendered from Designer templates, data import and export)
left_out.why: Listed in Adobe's Early Access Program.
left_out.quote: Forms service generates interactive PDF forms for data capture.

left_out.what: Power Automate flows on a GCC (government) tenant
left_out.why: Access goes through Adobe's Early Adopter Program. It matters for public sector clients on GovCloud.
left_out.quote: If you're on GovCloud and need to connect to a GCC (Government Cloud Computing) tenant, send an email from your official address to aem-forms-ea@adobe.com to request access through the Early Adopter Program.

left_out.what: Forms Portal drafts and submissions on storage other than Azure
left_out.why: Adobe documents Azure Storage only and asks clients who need another store to write to its early access address, so AFX02 assumes Azure.
left_out.quote: If you need to configure a storage option other than Azure, write to aem-forms-ea@adobe.com from your official email address with your detailed requirements.

left_out.what: Adobe Analytics through Experience Cloud Setup Automation
left_out.why: Adobe marks this route deprecated. AF09 uses the Tags route with the Adobe Experience Manager Forms extension.
left_out.quote: The Experience Cloud Setup Automation functionality is deprecated.

left_out.what: Acrobat Sign fields placed inside an adaptive form (in-form signing)
left_out.why: Not a lifecycle label, a documentation gap: the page that adds Acrobat Sign fields to a form is written for Foundation Components, and the notable changes page says the service does not support an in-form signing experience. AF08 signs through the Sign Document workflow step.
left_out.quote: The service does not support in-form signing experience and does not include the Summary and Verify components for Adaptive Form.

left_out.what: A form accessibility review as its own line
left_out.why: Not a lifecycle label, a documentation gap: the authoring steps (accessible names, labels, alternative text, contrast, keyboard access) are documented for Foundation Components, and the newer accessibility markup for Core Components sits in the Early Access list. Flagged for Adam because public sector clients will ask for it.
left_out.quote: While authoring an Adaptive Form, form authors must address the following considerations to build an accessible Adaptive Form
